the enantioseparations of the amine and aminoalcohols are possible on polysaccharide CSPs using acidic or basic additive in the mobile phases.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a basic additive (DEA) allows a better enantiomeric resolution of aromatic amines and a more acidic additive (TFA) of the aminoalcohol.
the best enantiosperation of the amine and of the aminoalcohol is achieved on amylose- and cellulose-based CSPs, respectively, in acidic conditions with TFA as additive.
the use of acidic or basic additive in the normal-phase mobile phase is an efficient tool for enantioseparations with polysaccharide CSPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the polysaccharide-based CSPs with acidic additive in the mobile phases are suitable for enantioresolution of a wide range of compounds, even if the separation of the enantioisomers of aromatic amines and aminoalcohols is possible only with acidic additive in normal-phase mode.
the use of acidic additives in the mobile phase is not recommended for the enantioseparations on polysaccharide CSPs, but basic additives are a good choice.

the use of a polysaccharide-based CSP in the normal phase mode and the addition of a small amount of a weak acid or a weak base to the mobile phase can be an effective approach to the separation of the enatiomers of aromatic amines and aminoalcohols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acidic additive is necessary to achieve the enantioseparations on the amylose-based CSP, while it is unnecessary on the cellulose-based CSP.

the use of an acidic additive in the mobile phases is an effective way to improve the enantioresolution of the enantiomer separation of aromatic amines and aminoalcohols on polysaccharide-based chiral stationary phases.
the enantiomeric separations of the studied compounds were possible with both acidic and basic additives, but the separation factors and resolution factors are higher in acidic conditions.
